title.narrative: Provision of winter repairs and winter NFIs to ensure safe living conditions for 1594 vulnerable displaced persons residing in 21 collective sites in Dnipropetrovska and Kharkivska oblasts

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThe project aims to ensure minimal safe living conditions in winter 2024/25 for 1594 of the most vulnerable internally displaced people in Dnipropetrovska and Kharkivska oblasts, including 511 pensioners, 122 persons with disabilities, 671 women, and 289 children. The intervention will provide winterization support to 21 collective sites, focusing on the provision of solid fuel, winter repairs and insulation, repair/upgrade of existing heating systems, as well as provision of solid fuel and alternative heating sources such as infrared heaters, oil heaters, fan heaters, charging stations, and buleryan stoves. Specifically, three collective sites, hosting 158 individuals, will receive insulation and small repairs carried out by Dobrobat, while 19 sites, hosting 1480 people, will receive in-kind winterization support organised by Angels of Salvation. The choice of these oblasts is driven by their high concentration of IDPs, with Dnipropetrovska hosting 14% and Kharkivska 12% of all displaced people in Ukraine (IOM DTM, April 2024). Mondo and its partners' long-term presence and winterization support experience in these regions further justify the selection.ltbrgtIn the design phase, Mondo along with sub-partners, leveraged our existing network of collective sites to consult equally with men and women of different ages female site managers equally played a key role in these consultations, ensuring that the intervention considers gender-specific needs. As a result, the project incorporates targeted protective actions for women and children, such as installing blinds during winter repairs to enhance privacy and security. ltbrgtThrough the joint rapid needs assessment conducted by Mondo and sub-partners in July 2024, specific needs of different sites and groups of residents were identified. Key findings produced as a result of consultations with site managers, field staff, and municipal authorities, indicated that 78% of sites lack sufficient heating sources, 63% cited poor insulation, and 83% highlighted limited access to certified, good-quality winter fuel. Most sites needing winter repairs identified windows as a primary issue for deficient thermal envelopes, requiring professional assistance for replacement. The assessment also revealed that 76% of sites preferred in-kind assistance over cash-based interventions due to logistical challenges, transportation capacity issues, procurement difficulties, and undesirable administrative burdens. Therefore, the project prioritises in-kind assistance, which will not only ensure that all items are carefully selected, but also delivered directly to the beneficiaries, eliminating the access-related bottlenecks. Together with Dorbobat’s volunteer building brigade in the region along with Angels of Salvation’s warehouses and transportation vehicles, the timely delivery of aid can be guaranteed.ltbrgtMonitoring data collection will be organised in stages (pre- and post-monitoring as well as two intermediate KIIs), extracting quantitative SADD and gathering qualitative feedback via questionnaires and story collection. A complaint and referral mechanism will ensure that any issues can be safely raised and Mondo stays prepared to swiftly address all potential complaints.ltbrgtlt/pgt
